audit.whatIsWrong: Four stages disagree with their own whys: Levels 2 and 3 read Gwen while both whys call them a coinflip, Levels 4-5 read even while the why and the spike call it 'his strongest window', Level 6 reads even while the why and spike say it flips to Gwen, and 2+ items reads Gwen while the why and the late text both say the matchup nets even.
audit.why: Hallowed Mist is the pivot and his CC never falls off — the honest shape is even early, his at 4-5, Gwen's from 6 through first item, even again late.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Skill / Skill / Nautilus / Gwen / Gwen / Skill in both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Dredge Line is called 'point-and-click' twice. It is a skillshot projectile, and the page never mentions that hooking TERRAIN pulls Nautilus to the wall.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Nautilus hurls his anchor forward. Colliding with an enemy pulls them and Nautilus together... Colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus towards it.' It can be dodged, it can be body-blocked by minions, and it doubles as a wall-hook escape — none of which is true of a point-and-click ability. Depth Charge genuinely is targeted, so only the hook wording was wrong.
audit.corrected: Hook described as a dodgeable skillshot; the terrain pull stated in Key Ability Interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Bait the hook' is the entire game plan and its cooldown appears nowhere.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10s — fourteen seconds at rank 1, the longest basic cooldown on either side of this lane, and the single most useful number here. Riptide is 7s, Titan's Wrath a flat 12s, Depth Charge 120/100/80s.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to the whys, spikes and cooldown breakdown.

edits.before: Still a coinflip — neither of you has a kill button yet, so deny the hook and farm even.
edits.after: Still a coinflip — no kill button yet, so sidestep the 14-second hook and farm even.

edits.after: Snip Snip! lets you poke and Skip 'n Slash resets it, but his 14-second hook into Riptide trades evenly back — nobody owns this stage outright.

edits.after: Your anti-tank DPS shreds his health, but Dredge Line and a targeted Depth Charge never fall off and can pin you out of mist — it nets even.

edits.after: Pre-6 his hook into Riptide and the Staggering Blow root out-stat you in a flat brawl — his strongest window, and Dredge Line is only 14s.

edits.before: This stays even because your strengths and his cancel out. Your %-max-HP Q and Thousand Cuts anti-tank profile shred everything Nautilus builds — the fatter his HP bar, the harder you hit and the more you heal. But his point-and-click CC never falls off: one Dredge Line hook or Depth Charge knockup pins you out of mist and lets his team delete you. Itemize to survive the catch, group with W up, and you out-DPS his entire frontline.
edits.after: This stays even because your strengths and his cancel out. Your %-max-HP Q and Thousand Cuts anti-tank profile shred everything Nautilus builds — the fatter his HP bar, the harder you hit and the more you heal. But his CC never falls off: one Dredge Line, which he can also hook off a wall to reposition, or one targeted Depth Charge pins you out of mist and lets his team delete you. Itemise to survive the catch, group with W up, and you out-DPS his whole frontline.

edits.before: Track Nautilus's Dredge Line (Hook): His only engage. Dodge it. When it is down — Snip him in your mist.
edits.after: Dredge Line (Q, 14s) is a dodgeable skillshot, and on terrain it pulls HIM to the wall — that is his escape too.

edits.before: - Nautilus Dredge Line: matchup-defining — His only engage. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Dredge Line (Q): 14/13/12/11/10s — a skillshot; sidestep it and you own fourteen seconds. - Riptide (E): 7s at rank 1. - Titan's Wrath: a flat 12s shield. - Depth Charge (R): 120/100/80s and targeted.

notes: Whether Hallowed Mist breaks an in-flight Dredge Line or a travelling Depth Charge is not answerable from the kit files — the page's existing 'drop W as the hook lands so the Riptide follow-up whiffs' framing was left as-is because it only claims the follow-up whiffs, which is safe.
